# Circulation sleeves
A circulation sleeve is packaging designed for at least five dispatch-and-return cycles.
## Admission
An undamaged sleeve is eligible for another dispatch after its fastener and label window pass inspection.
## Exception
A sleeve with a torn load seam is ineligible even when its fastener and label window pass.
fresh.question: Under the circulation-sleeve policy, what qualifies an item for that category, and can a sleeve pass the fastener and label-window checks yet remain ineligible for dispatch because its load seam is torn?
requirements: The defining design criterion for a circulation sleeve.
Dispatch eligibility when inspection checks pass but the load seam is torn.
fresh.residual: Definition and exception are supplied; a particular physical sleeve remains unverified. Passing two checks does not override the torn-seam exclusion.

The plan would compare sorting time with the existing route.
No parcels have been tested under this proposal.
No sorting times, accuracy rates, or uncertainty estimates are available.
fresh.question: For the proposed color-sorting pilot, what observed change in sorting time and error rate was measured against the current workflow, how many parcels contributed data, and what uncertainty accompanies those results?
requirements: Observed comparative sorting times and error rates.
Actual sample size and uncertainty for those observed results.

# Vent label timing
## Initial experiment
With 40 volunteers, the embossed vent label reduced median identification time from 8.0 to 6.2 seconds.
The median difference was -1.8 seconds; its bootstrap 95% interval was -2.5 to -1.0 seconds.
## Replication
A second laboratory tested 36 different volunteers and found 8.1 seconds with the standard label and 8.4 seconds with the embossed label.
Its median difference was +0.3 seconds, with a bootstrap 95% interval of -0.4 to +1.1 seconds.
The second study did not reproduce the initial speed improvement.
fresh.question: Across the initial embossed vent label experiment and a separate laboratory's replication, how many people were tested, what happened to identification time, and what uncertainty supports or challenges a consistent improvement?
requirements: Initial sample size, measured timing difference, and uncertainty.
Replication sample size, measured timing difference, and uncertainty, including disagreement with the initial result.
fresh.residual: Both studies supply measurements but not consistent improvement. No pooled estimate or explanation of disagreement is supplied.
